Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a member of the House of Antioch and ruled Tripoli from 1147 to 1171 he was the son of Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Helena of Armenia 

*Highlighting the Early Life and Succession* 
Raymond III was born around 1142 his father was killed in 1147 by the Assassins and he succeeded him as Count of Tripoli at the age of five his mother Helena acted as regent until 1150

Raymond III took part in the Siege of Kerak in 1170 alongside King Amalric I of Jerusalem and Prince Bohemond III of Antioch the siege was unsuccessful due to the arrival of Nur ad-Din 

He played a crucial role in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 where the Crusader army was defeated by Saladin Raymond III was captured and released after promising to pay a ransom and surrender Tripoli however he did not fulfill his promise 

*Highlighting the Regency and Marriage Plans*
Raymond III never married and had no children he was under the regency of his mother until 1150 and later under the tutelage of King Baldwin III of Jerusalem 

Raymond III was known for his bravery and chivalry he was also known for his conflicts with King Amalric I of Jerusalem over the governance of the Kingdom of Jerusalem 

*Highlighting the Later Life and Legacy*
Raymond III died in 1183 at the age of 41 the cause of his death is not certain he was succeeded by his cousin Bohemond IV of Antioch who united the County of Tripoli with the Principality of Antioch
